semantics: descriptor: quickLogFor(questions) decides eligibility (quicklog-vectors.json). Enum: {type: 'enum', key, label, options: [{value, label}], total_options}; with <= 4 active options all of them in question order, with 5-6 the 3 with the highest counts[value] (missing = 0), ties in question order. Number: {type: 'int'|'double', key, label, unit, min, max, decimals (null for int), last_value}.
Labels (question and option) and units are cut to 64 Unicode scalars, the last one replaced by '…'. An empty unit is null.

last_value: `last` (the latest numeric answer for the key, by captured_at then entry id) when the server would accept it as an answer to the question (type, bounds; a whole double counts as an int); else null. decimals is a display hint and never drops or rounds it. Ints stay ints, doubles are JSON doubles.

actions: enum: one {kind: 'log', identifier: q1|server|topic|version|key|o|value, title: label} per option, then {kind: 'open', identifier: ...|m|, title: 'More…'} when total_options > options.length. Number: when last_value != null, {kind: 'log', identifier: ...|n|fmt(last), title: '✓ ' + fmt(last) + (unit ? ' ' + unit : '')}; then {kind: 'input', identifier: ...|i|, title: 'Other value…', text_input_button_title: 'Log', text_input_placeholder: unit ? 'Value in ' + unit : 'Value'}.

category_id: 'quickr.t.' + topic_id + '.' + the first 16 lowercase hex digits of sha256(UTF-8(NFC(hash_input))). hash_input = 'quickr-cat-v1' + for each action: U+001E + kind + U+001F + identifier + U+001F + title (+ U+001F + button title + U+001F + placeholder for 'input'). hash_input is listed already NFC-normalised.
body_suffix: appended to the APNs alert body when options are cut: ' · {n} of {total} shown, More for all'.

fmt(kind, value): int: base 10. double: the shortest decimal that round-trips to the same binary64 value (JS String(x), Python repr), written positionally (no exponent), with no trailing zeros or dot; '0' for both zeros. No rounding: decimals is not used. Always '.', no grouping. `bits` is the double's IEEE 754 big-endian hex, to build it without a JSON parser.
